title: Sky above Paranal
caption: The Milky Way above the Very Large Telescope Interferometer, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: The Milky Way stretches grandly across this photograph from Paranal, with the Magellanic Clouds visible on the right. The foreground shows several of the docking stations used by the Auxiliary Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope Interferometer.

Almost at the centre of the image shines Alpha Centauri, the lower of the two Pointers that lead to the Southern Cross. They sit just above the dark patch known as the Coal Sack, a cloud of dust that blocks the light of the stars behind it. The photo looks towards the east.

There is a bonus, too: a shooting star streaks across the top right of the frame, caught in the brief moment it burned up. The image was taken on 11 December 2005 by Hännes Heyer of ESO, using a Canon EOS 5D camera with exposures of 40 and 20 seconds. The docking stations let the movable Auxiliary Telescopes be placed in different positions.

understand.summary: This photograph was taken with a Canon EOS 5D using 40- and 20-second exposures, as stated by ESO.
understand.eye: The exposures gather more light than the eye, so the Milky Way and Magellanic Clouds look brighter than they would in person.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: By moving the Auxiliary Telescopes between stations, astronomers can change how the interferometer combines their light.
alt: The Milky Way and Magellanic Clouds over Paranal, with telescope docking stations in the foreground and a shooting star at the top right.
